_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run (npm run check:golden sensory-minefield-mapper). v3.1 (2026-09-09) added 10 output-correction rules on top of the v3 rewrite (no compounded place-type possibilities, no place-type-as-fact framing, no unsupported mechanism claims, past-visit duration never restated as a forecast, supplied constraints preserved exactly rather than strengthened, no invented clock times, no generic reassurance, only-selected-or-necessary sensory factors, a 5-way KNOWN/PAST EXPERIENCE/POSSIBILITY/UNKNOWN/PREPARATION evidence model, and "THE VISITOR IS THE SENSOR" as the closing north star) plus a required, fixed-set travel-mode field for Route mode (was free text) with its own ROUTE MODE RULES section forbidding invented route/transit/traffic conditions. DO NOT reverse any of those, or the 7 new outputGuard.prohibit entries that back them. Real bug found and fixed during this pass, same failure class as ScamRadar v2.1 the same day: runOutputGuard mutates its `draft` argument IN PLACE, and its repair pass can blank out a flagged field instead of substituting it — despite the repair prompt explicitly saying not to. A stripEmptyItems() call made BEFORE runOutputGuard only catches blanks already in the raw model output, not ones the repair step introduces afterward; caught live via a route-mode call that came back with a populated `factor` and `prepare` array sitting next to a blank `what_might_matter`. Fix: run stripEmptyItems() AFTER runOutputGuard, not before, and drop an array-of-objects item if ANY of its own string fields is blank (not just when ALL of them are) — a half-populated object is exactly as useless as a fully-blank one. Do not move the stripEmptyItems() call back above runOutputGuard, and do not loosen the "every string field" check back to "some field" — both regressions were caught live in this exact session.

input.knownInfo: Appointment at 9:00 but told to arrive at 8:30. I cannot leave and come back — if my name is called and I am not there I go to the end of the line. Last time I waited about two hours.

summary.heading: Regional hospital, outpatient wing
summary.one_liner: You have a 9:00 appointment with an 8:30 arrival, and you need to stay within earshot the whole time.

what_you_know: Arrival time is 8:30 for a 9:00 appointment.
If your name is called and you are not present, you go to the end of the line — so you need to stay within earshot.
Your last visit involved about a two-hour wait.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: Outpatient waiting areas can have overhead announcements, background PA systems, other patients, and staff movement — the mix and volume vary by area and time.
prepare: Bring whatever hearing management you already use — earplugs, earcups, or earbuds — set at a level where you can still hear your name called.
If you use earbuds, keep one ear open or set a low enough volume that announcements come through.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: Some hospital waiting areas use overhead artificial lighting; the type and intensity vary and are not established for this specific room.
prepare: Bring sunglasses or a hat with a brim if bright overhead light is something you want the option to reduce.
If you have a preferred seat position relative to light sources, look at the room when you arrive and choose accordingly if there is a choice.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: Hospital environments may have cleaning products, hand sanitiser stations, or other clinical smells — what is present in this specific area is not known in advance.
prepare: If you have a scent you find neutral or grounding, bring a small amount on a tissue or cloth you can hold near your face.
Identify ahead of time whether there is any movement available to you within the permitted waiting area, so you have that option if one spot is more difficult than another.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: Climate control in waiting areas can run cooler or warmer than expected and may not be adjustable.
prepare: Wear or bring a layer you can add or remove easily.
A small water bottle can help if the air is dry.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: Because your last visit involved about a two-hour wait, today could be similar — though it may also differ.
prepare: Bring enough to occupy yourself for a potentially extended wait — reading, audio, a task on your phone — keeping the earpiece arrangement above in mind.
Charge your devices fully before you go, since a long wait can deplete a phone.

before_you_go: Pack everything the night before or well ahead of departure so you are not assembling it at the last minute.
Eat and hydrate before you arrive — you may be there for a while and may not want to leave the area for food or drink.
If you take any medication on a schedule, account for the possibility that you are still there at the next dose time.
while_youre_there: When you check in, confirm with staff what 'present when called' means in practice — whether there is any flexibility to step a short distance away, use a nearby bathroom, or move within a corridor — so you know your actual range of movement rather than assuming the most restrictive version.
Choose a seat where you are visible to staff and can hear announcements, then settle your comfort items from there.
If one part of the waiting area is noticeably more difficult than another, check with staff whether you can move to a different permitted spot before committing to a seat.

things_you_could_ask.situation: At check-in, before you settle in to wait.
things_you_could_ask.script: I need to make sure I hear my name when it is called. Is it okay if I sit anywhere in this waiting area, or should I stay in a particular spot? And is there anywhere nearby — like a hallway or bathroom — that I can step to briefly without losing my place?

things_you_could_ask.situation: If the environment is difficult and you want to know whether moving is an option.
things_you_could_ask.script: Is there another area I am allowed to wait in? I want to make sure I can still hear when I am called.

backup_plan: If noise becomes difficult, adjust your hearing management to the lowest reduction level that still lets you hear your name — prioritise staying in earshot over maximum comfort reduction.
If the lighting or smells in your current seat are difficult, ask staff whether you can move within the permitted waiting area before deciding you are stuck.

If you feel like you need a short mental break, consider what you can change from your seat — switching what you are listening to, closing your eyes, adjusting your layer — before doing anything that takes you out of hearing range.
unknowns_that_matter: What the actual range of permitted movement is — the check-in conversation will establish this and is worth having early.
Whether the waiting area has natural light, window seating, or any variation in lighting across the room.
Whether there are strong smells in this specific outpatient area on this visit.
How long today's wait will actually be — your past experience gives context but does not determine today.

input.knownInfo: Er sagte: "Es ist meistens sehr laut nach der Arbeit."

summary.heading: Supermarkt um die Ecke
summary.one_liner: Du weißt bereits, dass es nach der Arbeit meistens sehr laut ist – der Plan geht davon aus, dass das heute wieder so sein könnte.

what_you_know: Nach deiner Erfahrung ist der Supermarkt nach der Arbeit meistens sehr laut.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: Du hast selbst erlebt, dass es nach der Arbeit meistens sehr laut ist.
prepare: Nimm Ohrstöpsel oder Kopfhörer mit – auch ohne Musik können sie den Geräuschpegel dämpfen.
Überleg vorher, was du brauchst, damit du dich kürzer im lautesten Bereich aufhalten musst.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: Du weißt, dass es laut ist – ob das auch mit mehr Menschen zusammenhängt, ist unklar.
prepare: Falls du eine Wahl hast, such dir die weniger belebte Kasse oder den Self-Checkout aus, wenn das für dich leichter ist.
Plane etwas Pufferzeit ein, falls Schlangen länger sind als erwartet.

before_you_go: Leg Ohrstöpsel oder Kopfhörer griffbereit – in die Jackentasche oder oben in die Tasche, damit du sie nicht suchen musst.
Schreib dir eine kurze Einkaufsliste, damit du dich im Laden auf das Wesentliche konzentrieren kannst.
while_youre_there: Wenn der Lärm belastend wird, mach eine kurze Pause – setz die Ohrstöpsel rein oder bleib kurz still, bevor du weitermachst.
Behalt im Blick, welche Kasse gerade am wenigsten besetzt wirkt, damit du nicht unnötig lange stehst.

things_you_could_ask.situation: Wenn du wissen möchtest, wann es erfahrungsgemäß ruhiger ist
things_you_could_ask.script: Entschuldigung, ich frage mich, ob es bestimmte Uhrzeiten gibt, zu denen hier weniger los ist – haben Sie da eine Einschätzung?

backup_plan: Wenn es zu laut oder zu voll ist: Setz die Kopfhörer auf oder steck die Ohrstöpsel rein, und konzentriere dich auf einen Schritt nach dem anderen – erst die Liste abarbeiten, dann zur Kasse.
Wenn die Situation unangenehm wird: Ohrstöpsel rein oder Kopfhörer auf, dann Schritt für Schritt weitermachen – erst das Nötigste kaufen, dann zur Kasse.
unknowns_that_matter: Wie laut und voll es heute konkret sein wird – deine Erfahrung gilt für 'meistens', nicht für jeden Besuch.
Ob es Uhrzeiten gibt, zu denen es spürbar ruhiger ist – das wäre beim Personal zu erfragen.

input.knownInfo: The market is usually busiest right at opening.

route_summary.heading: Walk to downtown farmers market
route_summary.one_liner: A walking trip to the farmers market, with crowds and noise as the main things to prepare for.

what_you_know: You said the market is usually busiest right at opening.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: You said the market tends to be at its busiest right at opening, so if you arrive then, that is the density you would be walking into.
prepare: If arriving at opening is flexible, arriving slightly after the initial rush — based on your own sense of when it tends to thin out — may give you a different experience.
Once you arrive, you can assess which areas feel more or less crowded and adjust where you spend your time accordingly.
If you have a specific item to get, knowing in advance which vendor you need means you can move with more purpose and spend less time navigating the busiest areas.

worth_preparing_for.what_might_matter: You mentioned crowds and noise as things to prepare for. Noise at the market could come from various sources, but you would know best what you encounter based on your visits.
prepare: If noise is something you manage when it becomes overwhelming, having your usual approach accessible means you are not caught off guard.
Notice what the noise level is like when you first arrive and whether it changes as you move through different parts of the market.

before_you_leave: If there are specific times you have found work better at the market based on your past visits, planning around those may help.
If your list of what you need at the market is short, writing it down means less time spent in the busiest parts working out what you still need.
backup_plan: If the crowd or noise becomes too much once you are there, stepping to the outer edge or a corner of the market space — away from the densest vendor rows — gives you somewhere to pause without leaving entirely.
If you need to leave earlier than planned, anything on your list that you did not get could be noted for another visit or sourced elsewhere.
unknowns_that_matter: How long the opening rush typically lasts at this particular market — you would know better than anyone based on your past visits.
Whether the market has any quieter sections (for example, a perimeter away from a stage or main entrance) — something you could look for once you arrive.
Whether there is amplified sound (music, announcements) and where it is positioned.

input.originalPlanSummary: Planning around a 2-hour wait, cannot leave without losing place.

output.acknowledgment: You're reporting that the wait is running longer and the space is more crowded than you prepared for.
adjusted_plan: If you brought headphones or earplugs, now is a reasonable time to put them on — more people in the space likely means more ambient noise.
If you have something to occupy yourself, shift to it now rather than waiting until you feel worn down.
Ask a staff member or check with the desk about roughly where you are in the queue — knowing you have more time ahead lets you pace yourself rather than staying on alert for your name.

Ask whether you are permitted to wait just outside the immediate area (a hallway, a quieter corner nearby) while still being reachable when called — your constraint is about being present when your name comes up, not about staying in one exact spot.
If the crowding is making the noise harder to manage, consider whether any of your existing items — a jacket, a bag — can create a small buffer of personal space around you.
still_applies_from_before: The plan to stay within earshot when your name is called still applies — that constraint hasn't changed.
Anything you brought to occupy yourself during a long wait is still worth using.
output.if_still_hard: If noise and crowding together become difficult to manage where you are sitting, ask at the desk whether there is any permitted waiting spot nearby that tends to be quieter.

essentials.why: Having something to occupy yourself gives you an option if you need a distraction.
Gives you something to engage with that does not depend on a reliable connection

comfort_items.why: You listed noise as a concern; these give you an option if the environment is louder than you want

Keeps your device available for as long as you need it.

comfort_items.item: Something to read or do offline
comfort_items.why: A backup that does not depend on battery or connection

just_in_case.why: Hospitals often run cool; having a layer you can add or remove gives you control over your comfort.

output.quick_note: Pack your bag the day before so you are not assembling it just before you leave — easier to notice if something is missing.

look_for: quieter waiting areas with fewer people passing through
smaller or independent clinics that handle the same type of appointment
facilities where you can wait in your car and be called or texted when it is your turn
appointment slots at lower-traffic times as reported by the venue or your own past experience
outdoor or semi-outdoor waiting space as an option

telehealth consultation if the appointment type permits it
asking your referrer whether a smaller satellite clinic or community health centre can handle the same care
